title: Lexicographic normal form for degree-stable Boolean functions
summary: Determine whether Boolean functions with no degree-drop hyperplane admit a canonical lexicographic normal form under affine changes of variables.

formal_statement.body: Write the degree-$r$ top support of $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2$ as $A\subseteq\binom{[n]}r$. A hyperplane is degree-dropping when the restriction of $f$ to it has degree below $r$. Assume no hyperplane is degree-dropping. Does an affine change of variables, modulo terms of degree below $r$, produce a support satisfying $\forall i\in\operatorname{Var}(A),\exists S\in A$ with $i\notin S$ and $S-t+i\notin A$ for every $t\in S$?

scope.domain: Degree stability and algebraic normal forms
assumptions: Degree-stability condition from the source paper
scope.unresolved_remainder: This record covers source Open Problem 1 only; the fast-point question is a separate record.
